title: Route visual feedback to a coding agent
promise: Turn a marked-up staging page into an agent task with a reviewable status trail.
whatItIs: CircleIt is described as a Chrome extension plus a Claude Code or Codex plugin. A teammate can mark an area on a page, explain the requested change, and send the screenshot, comment, and page metadata to a running coding agent. The source says the system matches the page address to a repository and reports status back in the sender's browser. A small student version could capture one staging page and open a proposed task for a developer's agent. Small product teams are a plausible customer, but that is a hypothesis. The loop handles intake and handoff; a human still needs to judge whether the requested change is correct and review code before release.
whoPays: Hypothesis: small software teams that collect frequent website feedback may pay; no customer or payment evidence is given.
loop: A teammate opens a staging page and marks a visible issue.
Capture the screenshot, comment, page address, and relevant metadata.
Match the page address to a configured repository.
Send the feedback to the team's running coding agent after any required approval.
Show the sender the agent's status and response.
A developer reviews code changes and decides whether to merge.
evidence: The Show HN author describes a Chrome extension and Claude Code/Codex plugin, screenshot and comment transfer to a running agent, address-based repository routing, status updates, and optional approval requirements for people or sites. The author reports a time improvement for their own small UI changes; this is an attributed personal claim.
uncertainty: The workflow is based on the maker's account and does not independently establish reliability or adoption. For a student MVP, limit access to a test repository and staging site. Address matching can route incorrectly, and agent-generated changes need human review before deployment.
first24Hours: Create a disposable demo page and test repository with one visible UI issue.
Build a browser capture form for a marked region, comment, and page URL.
Route one captured report to a task queue and add a manual approval step before an agent receives it.

claimChecks.claim: CircleIt lets a user mark up a web page in Chrome and send the feedback to a running Claude Code or Codex session.
claimChecks.evidenceQuote: Mark up any web page in Chrome and press Send. Your running Claude Code or Codex session wakes up

claimChecks.claim: CircleIt can keep feedback pending when no agent is running and pick it up when a session starts in that project.
claimChecks.evidenceQuote: If nothing is running, feedback stays pending until the next session starts in that project.

claimChecks.claim: CircleIt supports requiring approval before selected feedback is sent to a developer.
claimChecks.evidenceQuote: Set a person or a site to Needs approval. Their feedback waits until the owner or an approver approves it.
